title: Effectiveness of Deterministic Validation and Automated Repair for Reducing First-pass NetOps Misconfiguration
research_question: Can a pipeline combining a frozen deterministic configuration validator and an automated iterative repair loop (≤1 automated repair iteration per the registered adapter) reduce the first-pass misconfiguration rate of LLM-generated network configurations relative to plain LLM single-shot generation on a paired intent→configuration task set?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H1: The guarded pipeline (deterministic validator + automated repair) reduces the first-pass misconfiguration rate by at least 50% (relative) versus plain LLM single-shot generation on the paired task set.
H2: One or fewer automated repair iterations recover ≥75% of initially invalid configurations produced by the LLM generator.
exploratory_questions: E1: Which validator failure categories (reachability, ACL, routing, syntax) are most amenable to automated repair?
E2: How sensitive pipeline effectiveness is to validator coverage and transformation canonicalization choices (sensitivity analyses).
benchmark_scope: Paired intent→configuration tasks synthesized deterministically from the frozen topology seed list (N=300).
Vendor variants limited to the vendor templates enumerated in the frozen transformation/unit-test artifacts described in the preregistration.
secondary_estimands: absolute and relative reduction in misconfiguration (fail) rate
repair success rate among initially invalid outputs
distribution of repair iterations to success
sampling_plan: Paired within-task sampling. Fixed deterministic seed list of 300 task seeds (task IDs 0001–0300) produced by the frozen topology generator; each seed yields identical paired tasks for baseline and guarded arms. Inclusion: tasks whose generated intent parses to a valid intent template by the frozen prompt parser. Exclusion: any seed whose generated intent is uninterpretable by the frozen prompt parser; excluded seeds are deterministically replaced from a preregistered reserve list. All inclusions, exclusions, and replacements are recorded in the execution manifest.
power_and_precision_plan: Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Target effect: 50% relative reduction in first-pass misconfiguration rate (H1). For planning, assume baseline pass rate 0.40 (baseline fail 0.60); a 50% relative reduction in fail rate maps roughly to an increase in pass rate from 40%→70% (absolute +30%). With N=300 paired tasks, McNemar-based approximations indicate >80% power to detect absolute differences ≥0.20 at alpha=0.05 under conservative discordant assumptions. Exact power conditioned on observed discordant counts will be recomputed and recorded in the execution manifest. Sensitivity analyses: recompute power and report primary test under baseline pass rates 0.30, 0.40, and 0.50; report exact 95% CIs for observed absolute and relative reductions; use permutation-based paired tests if McNemar assumptions appear strained.
exclusion_rules: Deterministic exclusion of seeds whose generated intent is uninterpretable by the frozen prompt parser; replacement from preregistered reserve seeds.
Reject any generated configuration that fails to parse to a valid AST after canonicalization; affected seed replaced deterministically prior to inclusion.
missingness_plan: Record every failed model call and classify as API/provider failure or technical failure. Apply the registered adapter's preregistered retry policy (one retry allowed only per contract limits). Primary analysis will use the available_analysis_contract failed_call_treatments: 'complete_pair_primary' (drop pairs only if both calls failed) and sensitivity 'complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity' (treat any failed generation as a failure). All failed-call events, retries, and outcomes are logged in the execution manifest.
analysis_plan: Confirmatory analysis executed by the registered executor 'paired_binary_analysis_v1' computing the estimand 'paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline'. Primary test: exact McNemar test (alpha=0.05) on paired pass/fail outcomes, reporting absolute risk reduction with 95% CI. Analysis will run both preregistered failed_call_treatments: 'complete_pair_primary' and the sensitivity 'complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity' and report both. Secondary analyses: exact binomial CIs for repair success, stratified McNemar tests by topology complexity and vendor, and robust logistic regression for subgroup checks. Multiple secondary comparisons controlled by Benjamini–Hochberg FDR (q=0.05). All per-task artifacts and analysis code are output for reproducibility.
multiplicity_plan: Primary confirmatory test is a single paired hypothesis (H1). Secondary metrics (repair success, iteration counts, failure categories) are exploratory; reported p-values for secondary analyses are corrected using Benjamini–Hochberg FDR (q=0.05). No alpha-splitting of the primary test.

stopping_rule: Complete all planned pairs (N=300). Early stopping only permitted for bona fide infrastructure/provider failure exceeding the preregistered retry and recovery policy or if the capability-manifest model-call budget is exhausted; any early stop must be logged in the execution manifest with reason and timestamp. No data-dependent early stopping for efficacy is permitted.
